verses.text: There's nothing to gain from boasting, but I'll go on to visions and revelations from the Lord.
I know a man in Christ who was caught up to the third heaven fourteen years ago. Whether it was in his body or apart from his body, I don't know—God knows.
I know this man—whether in his body or apart from it, I don't know; God knows—
who was caught up into Paradise and heard things no one can express, things a person isn't allowed to repeat.
I'll boast about someone like that, but I won't boast about myself except in my weaknesses.
If I wanted to boast, I wouldn't be foolish, because I'd be telling the truth. But I won't, so no one will think more of me than what they see me do or hear me say.
To keep me from becoming conceited because of these extraordinary revelations, I was given a thorn in my flesh, a messenger of Satan to torment me and keep me from pride.
Three times I begged the Lord to take it away from me.
But he told me, ‘My grace is enough for you, because my power is made complete in weakness.’ So I'll gladly boast even more about my weaknesses, so Christ's power may rest on me.
That's why, for Christ's sake, I take pleasure in weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions, and difficulties. When I'm weak, then I'm strong.
I've been foolish to boast, but you pushed me to it. You should have commended me, because I'm in no way inferior to those so-called super-apostles, even though I am nothing.
The signs of a true apostle were done among you with great endurance—signs, wonders, and miracles.
How were you treated as less than the other churches, except that I wasn't a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong!

Look, I'm ready to visit you for a third time, and I still won't be a burden. I don't want what you own; I want you. Children shouldn't save up for their parents; parents should save up for their children.
I'll gladly spend everything I have and wear myself out for you. If I love you more, should you love me less?
Even so, I wasn't a burden to you. But some of you may say I was crafty and tricked you.
Did I take advantage of you through anyone I sent to you?
I urged Titus to go, and sent our brother with him. Did Titus take advantage of you? Didn't we act in the same spirit and follow the same steps?
Do you think we've been defending ourselves to you all this time? We speak in Christ before God. Dear friends, everything we do is to build you up.

I'm afraid that when I come I may not find you as I want, and you may not find me as you want. I'm afraid I'll find arguments, jealousy, anger, selfish ambition, slander, gossip, arrogance, and disorder.
I'm afraid that when I come again, my God will humble me before you, and I'll grieve over many who sinned before and haven't turned away from their impurity, sexual immorality, and reckless behavior.
